md_description: This workflow starts with airborne microbial material collected from urban locations in multiple cities and transforms it through preservation, nucleic-acid extraction, library preparation, and sequencing. It also captures site-level environmental observations such as latitude, longitude, time of day, weather, air quality, pollution context, and nearby land use to form a metadata table. The resulting sequence reads are processed into microbial community abundance summaries and then combined with environmental metadata to support analyses of how airborne microbial composition correlates with urban pollution sources and air quality.

airborne_microbial_sample.reasoning: For the root Entity node airborne_microbial_sample, I included only intrinsic sample identity and collection-origin properties that define what the sample is, not what was done to it or any later measurement outputs. Because this node is the source of the workflow and already underlies site_environment_observation, I avoided repeating site-level environmental metadata such as latitude, longitude, time of day, weather, air quality, and nearby land use, since those belong to the downstream observation/derivative nodes. I also avoided preservation, extraction, library, sequencing, signal, and analysis fields because those are owned by downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. Fields were limited to the minimum sample descriptors needed to identify and distinguish airborne particulate samples across cities and collection events.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the airborne particulate sample; use a stable string such as AIRSAMP_0001. Assigned at collection and used to link this root sample to downstream preservation, extraction, sequencing, and metadata records.

Identifier for the field collection event that yielded this sample; use a string format such as EVT_2026_05_17_003. Captures the sampling occasion for grouping replicate samples or co-collected materials.

Name of the urban area where the airborne sample was collected, recorded at the time of sampling; example values include 'Chicago' or 'Delhi'. Use this as a high-level origin label, distinct from exact coordinates which belong to the site metadata node.

Local site label or station name for the collection location, if available; for example 'Downtown rooftop site' or 'Park edge station'. Assigned during field collection to distinguish multiple sites within the same city.

Material class of the collected item, describing the physical nature of the root sample; for this workflow it should indicate airborne particulate matter containing microbial biomass. Record as a controlled categorical field.

Brief description of how the airborne sample was physically collected, such as active air filtration or passive capture. Record the method used for the sample itself, not the downstream preservation or processing protocol.
Duration of the airborne sample collection in minutes, measured during the field sampling event. Typical values are positive integers such as 15, 30, 60, or 1440, depending on sampler setup.
Replicate number for this sample within the site and collection event, if multiple airborne samples were taken under the same conditions. Use 1 for the first replicate, 2 for the second, and so on.

Free-text note on the observable condition of the collected sample at the moment of retrieval, such as visible debris load, filter overloading, or unusual discoloration. Use this for intrinsic collection-quality observations, not preservation or sequencing quality.

sample_preservation.reasoning: For the Process node sample_preservation, I included only fields that describe how the collected airborne sample was stabilized for downstream molecular work: protocol identity, preservation agent, temperature, duration, storage conditions, and whether the step succeeded. I excluded sample identity and collection-origin fields because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded extraction/library/sequencing outputs because those belong to downstream nodes. I also avoided generic environment observations because the process node should describe the operation performed on the sample, not the field conditions around sampling.

md_schema.descr: Name of the preservation protocol applied immediately after collection, for example 'RNA later stabilization' or 'dry ice transport protocol'. Record the protocol used to stabilize the airborne sample before nucleic-acid extraction.
Chemical or physical stabilizer used during preservation, if any, such as RNAlater, ethanol, liquid nitrogen, or cold storage only. Record the agent or strategy actually applied to the sample.

Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the sample was preserved or held during stabilization, measured during the preservation step. Typical values may range from -196 to 25 depending on cryogenic, refrigerated, or ambient preservation.

Elapsed time in minutes that the collected sample remained under the preservation condition before being transferred to downstream processing or storage. Typical values range from minutes to hours, such as 30, 120, or 1440.

Storage condition applied after preservation and before nucleic-acid extraction, for example 'frozen_at_-80C', 'refrigerated_4C', or 'ambient_short_term'. Record the condition that maintained sample stability between workflow steps.

Indicator of whether the preservation step completed successfully without obvious compromise to the sample. Record true when the sample was stabilized as intended and false when there was leakage, thawing, or other failure.

preserved_air_sample.reasoning: For the preserved_air_sample Entity node, I included only intrinsic state descriptors of the stabilized sample as it exists after preservation and before extraction. These fields capture the preserved sample identity, current storage state, handling history, and observable integrity/quantity, which are properties of the entity itself rather than the preservation process. I excluded protocol settings, preservation agent details, temperature, and duration because those belong to the upstream sample_preservation Process node, and I excluded extraction/library/sequencing fields because those are downstream operations or outputs. I also avoided repeating the root sample identifiers already generated elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the stabilized airborne sample as stored after preservation; use a stable string such as PSAMP_0001. Assigned when the sample is transferred into its preserved state and used for downstream tracking.

Physical storage location for the preserved sample at the time it is ready for nucleic-acid extraction, such as freezer, rack, box, or transport container label. Record the sample's current holding location, not the file or database path.

Current storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the preserved sample immediately before extraction. Typical values range from -196 to 25 depending on cryogenic, frozen, refrigerated, or short-term ambient storage.

Total time in hours that the sample has spent in preserved storage before extraction is initiated. Use this as a sample-state attribute at the time the preserved entity is accessioned for the next step; typical values may range from fractions of an hour to many days.
Qualitative integrity status of the preserved sample immediately before nucleic-acid extraction. Record whether the sample appears intact and usable after preservation handling.

Estimated amount of preserved material available for extraction, measured as the quantity of collected airborne biomass or retained material. Use the unit appropriate to the workflow measurement, such as micrograms of material or number of filters if the sample is filter-based; typical values depend on collection yield.

nucleic_acid_extraction.reasoning: For the nucleic_acid_extraction Process node, I included fields that describe how microbial nucleic acids were isolated from the preserved airborne sample: extraction protocol, kit/reagent used, input material amount, elution conditions, yield, and a brief purity indicator. I excluded preserved-sample identity and storage attributes because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded DNA identity or downstream library/sequencing details because those belong to the extracted_dna entity and later nodes. I also avoided repeating preservation parameters already generated for the sample_preservation step, focusing instead on the extraction operation itself and its immediate output quality.

md_schema.descr: Name of the nucleic-acid extraction protocol used on the preserved airborne sample, for example 'bead-beating silica column extraction' or a kit-specific workflow. Record the exact method applied during this process step.

Commercial kit or in-house reagent system used for nucleic-acid extraction, if applicable, such as a silica spin-column kit or magnetic bead system. Record the kit actually used for this extraction run.

Amount of preserved sample material loaded into the extraction workflow, measured at the start of extraction. Typical values may be expressed in sample-specific units such as filter fraction, microliters of lysate, or mass equivalents; use the value appropriate to the workflow.
Final elution volume in microliters used to recover nucleic acid from the extraction matrix at the end of the process. Typical values are often 20 to 100 microliters.

Mass of recovered nucleic acid in nanograms measured after extraction and before library preparation. Record the yield obtained from this process step; typical values may range from below 1 ng to several hundred ng depending on sample biomass.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 for the extracted nucleic acid, measured after extraction as a basic quality indicator. Typical values for relatively pure DNA are around 1.8, though values can vary with sample type and assay conditions.

Indicator of whether the extraction process completed successfully and produced usable nucleic acid for downstream library preparation. Record true when extract recovery met workflow expectations and false when the process failed or produced insufficient material.

extracted_dna.reasoning: For the extracted_dna Entity node, I included intrinsic properties of the purified DNA as a material object after extraction and before library preparation: DNA identifier, concentration, total mass, fragment length, purity, and integrity status. I excluded extraction protocol, kit, and elution settings because those belong to the upstream nucleic_acid_extraction Process node, and I excluded library construction and sequencing settings because those are downstream. I also avoided repeating sample-level identity or preservation information generated earlier in the DAG, keeping this node focused on the DNA entity itself and its measurable quality state.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified DNA entity recovered from the airborne microbial sample; use a stable string such as DNA_0001. Assigned after extraction and used to track the DNA into library preparation.

Concentration of purified DNA in nanograms per microliter measured after extraction and before library preparation. Typical values may range from below 0.1 ng/µL to hundreds of ng/µL depending on biomass and recovery.

Total amount of purified DNA recovered from the extraction, expressed in nanograms. Measure this after extraction and before any dilution or library preparation; typical values can range from sub-ng to several hundred ng.

Approximate dominant DNA fragment length in base pairs measured on the purified DNA prior to library preparation, for example from electrophoresis or capillary assay. Typical values may range from a few hundred bp to many kilobases depending on extraction quality.
Spectrophotometric purity ratio A260/A280 for the purified DNA, measured after extraction as a basic contamination indicator. Typical values for clean DNA are around 1.8.
Qualitative assessment of DNA integrity at the time it enters library preparation. Record whether the DNA is intact, moderately fragmented, or heavily fragmented/compromised.

library_preparation.reasoning: For the library_preparation Process node, I included only fields that describe how extracted DNA was converted into a sequencing-ready library: library preparation protocol, kit, input DNA amount, insert size target, amplification cycles, indexing strategy, and a preparation success indicator. I excluded DNA identity and quality fields because those belong to the upstream extracted_dna Entity node, and I excluded sequencer settings and raw file characteristics because those belong to the downstream sequencing_capture and raw_reads nodes. I also avoided duplicating extraction protocol details already generated for nucleic_acid_extraction, keeping the focus on the library construction operation and its immediate output quality.

md_schema.descr: Name of the library preparation protocol used to convert extracted DNA into a sequencing-ready library, for example a shotgun metagenomic library workflow or a kit-specific protocol. Record the exact procedure applied in this process step.
Commercial library preparation kit or in-house reagent system used for constructing the sequencing library, if applicable. Record the kit actually used for this run.

Amount of extracted DNA input into the library preparation reaction, measured in nanograms at the start of this step. Typical values may range from 0.1 to 100 ng depending on assay design and biomass yield.

Target insert size in base pairs for the sequencing library generated during preparation. Record the intended fragment size range chosen during the library construction step; typical values may range from about 150 to 800 bp.

Number of PCR amplification cycles used during library preparation, measured for this process step if amplification was performed. Typical values often range from 0 to 18 cycles depending on input DNA amount.
Indexing or barcoding strategy used to label the library for multiplex sequencing, such as single-index, dual-index, or unique dual-index. Record the strategy applied during library preparation.

Indicator of whether the library preparation step completed successfully and produced a sequencing-ready library. Record true when the library met expected quality and quantity requirements, and false otherwise.

sequencing_library.reasoning: For the sequencing_library Entity node, I included intrinsic properties of the prepared library as a material entity after library construction and before sequencing: library identifier, concentration, fragment size distribution, adapter/index composition, molarity, and QC status. I excluded library preparation protocol, input DNA amount, and amplification settings because those belong to the upstream library_preparation Process node, and I excluded sequencer model, run settings, and raw file characteristics because those belong to the downstream sequencing_capture and raw_reads nodes. I also avoided repeating DNA-source identity fields already established earlier in the DAG, focusing on the library itself and its readiness for capture.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared sequencing library; use a stable string such as LIB_0001. Assigned after library preparation and used to track the library into sequencing.

Concentration of the prepared sequencing library in nanograms per microliter measured before loading onto the sequencer. Typical values may range from below 0.1 to tens of ng/µL depending on library type and cleanup.
Molar concentration of the prepared library in nanomolar measured prior to sequencing loading. Typical values often range from 1 to 20 nM for many Illumina-style workflows.

Observed modal fragment size in base pairs for the prepared library, measured after library construction and before sequencing. Typical values are often between 200 and 600 bp for short-read sequencing libraries.
Type of adapter/index architecture present in the library, indicating how reads will be demultiplexed after sequencing. Record the library's indexing design as prepared for sequencing.

Qualitative readiness status of the prepared library immediately before sequencing. Record whether the library passed size, concentration, and contamination checks sufficient for loading onto the instrument.

sequencing_capture.reasoning: For the sequencing_capture Capture node, I included instrument configuration and run-session settings that are actively controlled during sequencing: manufacturer/model/serial, platform, run mode, read structure, read lengths, chemistry/kit, lane or flow-cell identifiers, and key run QC indicators. I excluded sample, DNA, and library properties because those belong upstream to Entity nodes, and I excluded file format, file size, and read counts because those belong to the downstream raw_reads Signal node. I also avoided repeating software pipeline fields, since this node is about the physical capture session and instrument configuration rather than computational processing.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session, recorded for the active sequencer that produced the raw reads; example values include 'Illumina' or 'Thermo Fisher'.
Model name of the sequencing instrument used during this capture session, for example 'MiSeq', 'NextSeq 2000', or similar. Record the exact model configured for the run.

Serial number of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session; use the manufacturer-assigned device identifier such as SN12345. Record this to distinguish among instruments with the same model.
Sequencing platform family used during capture, describing the instrument technology rather than the sample. Typical values should correspond to the active sequencer class used in this workflow.
Operational mode of the sequencing session, such as single-end or paired-end read capture. Record the mode configured on the instrument for this run.

Configured read length in base pairs for each sequencing read in this capture session, measured as the intended output length set on the instrument. Typical values may range from 75 to 300 bp for short-read platforms.
Description of the sequencing read structure used during capture, such as '2x150 bp' or '1x250 bp'. Record the instrument output structure configured for this run.
Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit used during the capture session, for example a specific flow-cell and reagent set. Record the exact chemistry applied to the instrument run.

Identifier of the flow cell or equivalent consumable used for this sequencing run; use a vendor or lab-assigned string such as FC123456. Record the physical capture consumable associated with the run.
Qualitative outcome of the sequencing capture session based on instrument-level run quality metrics. Record whether the run passed, was borderline, or failed before downstream processing.

raw_reads.reasoning: For the raw_reads Signal node, I included properties of the raw data artefact itself: file identity and location, file format, size, read count, base count, quality encoding, and basic file-level QC metrics. I excluded sequencing instrument settings and chemistry because those belong to the upstream sequencing_capture Capture node, and I excluded trimming, demultiplexing, or interpretation because those belong to downstream processing or derivative nodes. I also avoided sample and library identifiers already created earlier, keeping the focus on the technical characteristics of the raw FASTQ-like file produced by the capture step.

md_schema.descr: Storage path or URI for the raw sequencing file produced by the capture run; use a string such as 's3://bucket/run1/sampleA_R1.fastq.gz' or a local path. Record the location of the raw FASTQ-like artefact.
File format of the raw sequence data artefact, for example FASTQ, FASTQ.GZ, BCL, or equivalent. Record the format as delivered by the sequencing instrument or primary output system.
Size of the raw reads file in bytes, measured for the stored artefact after sequencing. Typical values may range from millions to billions of bytes depending on run depth and compression.

Total number of raw reads contained in the file or run output, counted before any trimming, filtering, or demultiplexing by downstream processing. Typical values can range from thousands to hundreds of millions.

Total number of nucleotide bases represented in the raw reads artefact before processing, measured across all reads in the file. Typical values depend on read length and depth and may range from 10^6 to 10^11 bases.
Phred quality score encoding used in the raw FASTQ-like file, such as standard Sanger/Phred+33 encoding. Record the encoding scheme present in the file.
Mean per-base quality score across all reads in the raw file, calculated from the raw artefact before any processing. Typical values for good runs often fall in the high 20s to 30s.

Basic file-level quality flag for the raw reads artefact, reflecting whether the data appear usable before downstream processing. Record pass, warning, or fail based on run-level metrics such as yield and base quality.

read_processing.reasoning: For the read_processing Process node, I included only fields that describe how raw reads were demultiplexed and cleaned: processing pipeline name/version, trimming and filtering settings, demultiplexing strategy, host/contaminant removal, retained read counts, and a processing success indicator. I excluded raw file properties such as file path and size because those belong to the upstream raw_reads Signal node, and I excluded taxonomic outputs and abundance summaries because those belong to the downstream processed_reads Signal and taxonomic_profiling Process nodes. I also avoided repeating sequencing instrument settings or library construction details, keeping the focus on the computational transformation applied to the raw reads.

md_schema.descr: Name of the read processing pipeline used to demultiplex and clean the raw sequencing reads, for example a workflow or command-line pipeline name. Record the exact software workflow applied in this process step.
Version of the read processing pipeline used on the raw reads, recorded at the time of processing. Use a stable version string such as '1.0.3' or a git tag if applicable.
Strategy used to assign reads to samples during processing, such as barcode-based demultiplexing or instrument-native sample splitting. Record the method applied before downstream analysis.
Number of adapter bases removed from the raw reads during processing, measured across the dataset or per read as implemented by the pipeline. Typical values range from 0 to tens of bases.
Phred score threshold used to trim low-quality bases from reads during processing. Typical values often range from 20 to 30.
Minimum read length in base pairs required for a read to be retained after cleaning and filtering. Typical values may range from 30 to 100 bp depending on the assay.
Method used to remove non-target or contaminant reads during processing, such as host subtraction or reference-based filtering. Record the strategy applied in this workflow step.
Number of reads retained after demultiplexing, trimming, and filtering, measured at the end of this process step and before downstream taxonomic profiling. Use this as a basic output yield indicator.

Indicator of whether the read processing step completed successfully and produced usable cleaned reads for downstream analysis. Record true when the pipeline finished without critical errors and false otherwise.

processed_reads.reasoning: For the processed_reads Signal node, I included only file-level and artefact-level properties of the cleaned read output: storage location, file format, file size, read count, length distribution, and a quality summary flag. I excluded the demultiplexing and trimming parameters because those belong to the upstream read_processing Process node, and I excluded taxonomic assignments or abundance estimates because those belong to downstream profiling and derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating raw-read fields when possible, focusing on the characteristics of the processed data object itself as the output artefact ready for taxonomic profiling.

md_schema.descr: Storage path or URI for the cleaned, demultiplexed reads file produced by read processing; use a string such as 's3://bucket/run1/sampleA_clean.fastq.gz'. Record the location of the processed read artefact.
File format of the processed reads artefact, for example FASTQ, FASTQ.GZ, or equivalent cleaned-read container. Record the format of the output file ready for taxonomic profiling.
Size of the processed reads file in bytes after trimming, filtering, and demultiplexing. Typical values depend on sequencing depth and read retention and may range from megabytes to many gigabytes.
Total number of reads retained in the processed reads file after cleaning and filtering, counted before taxonomic profiling. This is the usable read yield passed to downstream analysis.

Typical retained read length in base pairs after trimming and filtering, measured on the processed read artefact. Report the modal or mean usable length, typically between 30 and 300 bp depending on the workflow.

Summary quality status for the processed reads artefact after cleaning, such as whether read quality and retention are sufficient for taxonomic profiling. Use a controlled categorical assessment of the final processed file.

taxonomic_profiling.reasoning: For the taxonomic_profiling Process node, I included only fields that describe the computational method used to assign processed reads to taxa and summarize community composition: profiling software, version, reference database, classification mode, assignment thresholds, and a profiling success indicator. I excluded processed-read file properties because those belong to the upstream processed_reads Signal node, and I excluded the abundance matrix itself because that belongs to the downstream community_abundance_table Derivative node. I also avoided repeating read-processing parameters or sequencing settings, keeping the scope on the profiling transformation from cleaned reads to taxon assignments.

md_schema.descr: Name of the taxonomic profiling software or pipeline used to assign processed reads to microbial taxa, for example a classifier or metagenomic profiler. Record the exact software applied in this process step.
Version of the taxonomic profiling software used for assignment of processed reads to taxa. Use a stable version string such as '2.1.0' or a release tag if applicable.
Name of the reference database used for taxonomic assignment, such as a curated microbial genome or marker-gene database. Record the exact database used during profiling.
Method used by the profiling software to assign reads to taxa, such as k-mer based classification, marker-gene mapping, or alignment-based placement. Record the method used in this workflow step.

Minimum confidence or probability threshold required for a read to be assigned to a taxon during profiling. Typical values are between 0 and 1 for probabilistic methods or method-specific cutoffs for other classifiers.
Taxonomic rank targeted for the primary output of the profiling step, such as species, genus, family, or order. Record the level at which community composition was estimated in this workflow.

Indicator of whether the taxonomic profiling step completed successfully and produced usable assignments for downstream abundance summarization. Record true when the profiling run finished without critical errors and false otherwise.

community_abundance_table.reasoning: For the community_abundance_table Derivative node, I included only computed-result fields that characterize the abundance matrix itself: table identifier, taxonomic rank, dimensions, sparsity, normalization method, abundance unit, and a result-quality indicator. I excluded profiling software, reference database, and assignment thresholds because those belong to the upstream taxonomic_profiling Process node, and I excluded raw or processed read properties because those belong to upstream Signal nodes. I also avoided site-environment metadata because those are captured in the separate site_metadata_table derivative and later integrated analysis node. The fields focus on the structure, scaling, and usability of the computed community composition matrix.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the community abundance table artifact; use a stable string such as ABUND_0001. Assigned when the taxonomic profiles are converted into a taxon-by-sample matrix.
Taxonomic rank at which counts or relative abundances are summarized in the table, such as genus or species. Record the primary rank used in the matrix.

Number of taxonomic features represented as rows in the abundance matrix, measured after profiling aggregation. Typical values may range from tens to thousands depending on the chosen rank and database.

Number of samples represented as columns in the abundance matrix, measured after merging taxonomic profiles across samples. This should match the number of profiled airborne samples included in the analysis.

Type of values stored in the abundance matrix, indicating whether entries are raw counts, relative abundances, or transformed values. Record the computed quantity represented in each cell of the table.

Normalization or scaling method applied to the taxon-by-sample matrix, if any, such as library-size scaling, compositional normalization, or total-sum scaling. Record the method used to produce the final table.
Proportion of non-zero cells in the abundance matrix, calculated after table construction. Typical values range from 0 to 1 and describe sparsity of the computed community data.

Overall quality flag for the computed abundance table, indicating whether the matrix is complete and suitable for downstream ecological analysis. Record pass, warning, fail, or unknown based on table validation checks.

site_environment_observation.reasoning: For the site_environment_observation Process node, I included only the observed and measured site-context variables collected during the field session: exact coordinates, city/site context, time of day, weather, air quality, pollution context, and nearby land use/proximity descriptors. I excluded sample identity and preservation details because those belong to the upstream sample Entity and preservation Process nodes, and I excluded the computed site_metadata_table output because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided sequencing-related fields entirely, since this node's territory is the field observation session that generates environmental covariates for later ecological analysis.

md_schema.descr: Latitude of the airborne sampling location in decimal degrees, recorded at the time of the field observation session. Typical values range from -90 to 90; use GPS or equivalent site measurement captured during sampling.

Longitude of the airborne sampling location in decimal degrees, recorded at the time of the field observation session. Typical values range from -180 to 180; use GPS or equivalent site measurement captured during sampling.
Name of the city where the site observation and sample collection occurred, recorded during the field session. Example values include city names such as 'Chicago' or 'London'.

Local site label or field station name assigned to the observation location, such as a rooftop, park edge, street canyon, or monitoring station identifier. Use this to distinguish multiple sites within a city.

Date and local time when the site observation and airborne sampling were recorded, captured at the moment of sampling. Use a full timestamp such as '2026-05-17T14:30:00' in local time; this is the measurement point for environmental covariates.

Categorical description of the local time window during sampling, recorded during the observation session to support comparisons across diurnal periods. Use the classification that best matches the collection time.
Dominant weather condition observed at the time of sampling, such as clear, cloudy, rain, snow, or fog. Record the field-observed weather state during the observation session.
Ambient air temperature in degrees Celsius at the sampling site when observations were recorded. Typical urban field values may range from below -20 to above 40 depending on season and climate.
Relative humidity percentage measured at the sampling site during the observation session. Typical values range from 0 to 100 and should reflect the local ambient condition at sampling time.

Air Quality Index value recorded for the sampling site or nearest official monitoring source at the time of sampling. Record the numerical index used in the local jurisdiction; typical values depend on the regional scale.

Qualitative pollution level at the sampling site during the observation session, summarized from air quality and/or local field assessment. Use a controlled category to reflect the site's pollution context.

Qualitative or categorical descriptor of how close the sampling site is to an industrial area, assessed during field observation or from local land-use context. Use a coarse category describing proximity at sampling time.

Qualitative or categorical descriptor of how close the sampling site is to a park, urban forest, or other green space, assessed during field observation or site context review. Use a coarse category describing proximity at sampling time.

Dominant surrounding land-use context at the sampling location, recorded during the observation session; examples include residential, commercial, industrial, park, mixed_use, or transportation corridor. Use the category that best represents the immediate environment.

Free-text notes captured during field observation about local conditions that may affect airborne microbial sampling, such as traffic intensity, construction, nearby vegetation, or unusual weather events. Use this for contextual details not captured by the structured fields above.

site_metadata_table.reasoning: For the site_metadata_table Derivative node, I included only computed table properties and the standardized environmental covariates that are assembled from site_environment_observation into a reusable metadata table: table identifier, row/column counts, coordinate fields, temporal/weather descriptors, air quality and pollution summaries, and proximity/land-use fields. I excluded raw field-notes and instrument session details because those belong to the upstream observation Process node, and I avoided sequencing or abundance outputs because those belong elsewhere in the DAG. Since the downstream integration step joins this table with community abundance data, I focused on the table’s structure and the harmonized site-level variables it contains.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed site metadata table artifact; use a stable string such as SITE_META_0001. Assigned when field observations are standardized into a table for downstream ecological analysis.

Number of site records contained in the metadata table, counted after standardization and any deduplication. This should correspond to the number of sampled locations or observation events represented.

Number of columns in the computed site metadata table, measured after assembly of the standardized environmental covariates. This count reflects the number of stored metadata variables included in the table.
Indicator of whether the computed metadata table includes a latitude column for sampling location. Record true when decimal-degree latitude is present in the table.
Indicator of whether the computed metadata table includes a longitude column for sampling location. Record true when decimal-degree longitude is present in the table.
Indicator of whether the computed metadata table includes a standardized time-of-day field. Record true when the table contains a categorical or derived time window variable for each site.
Indicator of whether the computed metadata table includes a weather condition field. Record true when the table contains a standardized categorical weather descriptor.
Indicator of whether the computed metadata table includes an air quality index variable. Record true when the table contains a numeric AQI column or equivalent local-scale air quality metric.
Indicator of whether the computed metadata table includes a pollution level category. Record true when the table contains a standardized pollution summary variable such as low, moderate, or high.
Indicator of whether the computed metadata table includes a proximity-to-industrial-area field. Record true when a standardized proximity category is present for each site.
Indicator of whether the computed metadata table includes a proximity-to-green-space field. Record true when a standardized proximity category is present for each site.

Overall quality flag for the computed site metadata table, indicating whether fields are complete, standardized, and ready for downstream join operations. Record pass, warning, fail, or unknown based on validation of the assembled table.

community_environment_join.reasoning: For the community_environment_join Process node, I included only fields describing the integration operation itself: join software, version, join key(s), join type, matched sample count, unmatched count, and join success. I excluded the actual abundance matrix and site metadata contents because those belong to the upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final combined analysis table because that belongs to the downstream urban_microbiome_analysis Derivative node. I also avoided repeating sequencing or environmental measurement details; this node is specifically about how two prepared tables are merged for analysis.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis workflow used to merge microbial abundance data with site metadata, for example a statistical or data-frame join tool. Record the exact software used for this integration step.
Version of the join software or workflow used for combining the abundance table and site metadata table. Use a stable version string such as '1.0.0' or a release tag if applicable.
Name of the field used to match microbial abundance records to site metadata records, such as sample_id or site_id. Record the primary join key used to integrate the two tables.
Type of relational join performed between abundance and site metadata tables, describing how unmatched records were handled. Record the join behavior used in this integration step.
Number of records successfully matched across the abundance and site metadata tables during the join operation. Measured after integration and before any downstream filtering or analysis.
Number of records that could not be matched during the join operation, counted across either table as applicable. Use this as a basic integration quality indicator for the merge step.

Indicator of whether the integration of abundance and site metadata completed successfully and produced a usable combined table for downstream ecological analysis. Record true when the join ran without critical errors and false otherwise.

urban_microbiome_analysis.reasoning: For the urban_microbiome_analysis Derivative node, I included only computed-result properties of the final integrated analysis dataset: analysis table identifier, row and column counts, analysis scope, statistical method, covariate set, summary metric type, effect-size summary, significance threshold, and an overall analysis quality flag. I excluded the underlying abundance and site metadata fields because those belong to upstream derivative nodes and the join process, and I excluded software runtime or join mechanics because those belong to upstream Process nodes. I focused on fields that let a downstream user understand what the integrated dataset contains, how it was summarized, and whether it is ready for ecological interpretation across cities.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the integrated urban microbiome analysis dataset; use a stable string such as UMA_0001. Assigned when community composition is combined with environmental covariates into the final analysis artefact.
Number of integrated records in the final analysis dataset, counted after merging abundance and site covariates. This should reflect the number of sample-level analysis rows available across cities.

Number of columns in the integrated analysis dataset, counted after assembly of microbial and environmental variables. This reflects the total number of fields available for downstream modeling or exploration.

Description of the primary scope of the integrated dataset, indicating whether it is organized for cross-city comparison, site-level correlation, or broader urban ecological modeling. Record the intended analysis framing of the final table.

Primary statistical or analytical method used to summarize the relationship between microbial composition and environmental covariates in the integrated dataset, if applicable. Record the method used to generate the final analysis artefact.

Name or label for the environmental covariate set included in the integrated analysis dataset, such as a predefined group of air quality and land-use variables. Record the covariate bundle used in the final artefact.

Type of microbial summary metric included in the integrated dataset, such as relative abundance, normalized abundance, diversity index, or composite community score. Record the principal community measure represented in the analysis table.

Summary of the main association strength reported or stored in the integrated dataset, such as a correlation coefficient, regression coefficient, or model effect size. Record the principal effect-size representation if the analysis produces one.

Statistical significance threshold applied in the integrated analysis, if one was used for reporting or filtering results. Typical values are 0.05 or adjusted thresholds such as 0.1 depending on the analysis design.

Overall quality flag for the final integrated analysis dataset, indicating whether the merged microbial-environment table is complete and suitable for downstream interpretation. Record pass, warning, fail, or unknown based on validation of the final artefact.
